title: Sensex Surges 879 Points as IT Stocks Lead Broad-Based Market Rebound
excerpt: The Sensex and Nifty each gained more than 1% on Friday, led by a 3% IT rally on strong TCS results — but persistent FII selling and Monday's CPI print will decide if the bounce holds.
body:
• The BSE Sensex climbed 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to close at 72,472.33 on Friday, while the Nifty 50 rose 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to 22,520.45 — snapping a two-session losing streak and recovering a significant portion of Thursday's steep losses.
  • Information technology led the recovery: the Nifty IT index jumped more than 3% as TCS, Infosys, and HCL Technologies rallied on TCS's September-quarter results (profit up 15% to ₹13,884 crore), with investors shrugging off the US green-card program suspension.
  • Easing global crude prices — Brent retreating below $103 a barrel from highs above $105 — and reduced fears of a US-Iran escalation supported sentiment, while 2,516 stocks advanced against 1,867 decliners in one of the session's broadest rallies.
  • What to watch: domestic CPI data lands Monday, testing the market's read of the RBI's calibrated-tightening shift; technicians peg Nifty support at 22,450 then 22,300, with resistance at 22,600 — a sustained breakout above it could extend the recovery toward 22,800.

A Relief Rally, Broad and Fast

Indian equities staged a decisive rebound on Friday, ending a two-day selloff that had erased more than 1,045 points from the Sensex on Thursday alone. The BSE benchmark gained 879.09 points to close at 72,472.33, touching an intraday high of 72,669.20, while the NSE Nifty 50 advanced 288.65 points to 22,520.45. The rally added more than ₹4 lakh crore to the combined market capitalization of BSE-listed companies, taking it to nearly ₹465 lakh crore. For the week, the Sensex gained 562.63 points (0.78%) and the Nifty rose 98.5 points (0.43%).

The recovery was broad-based. The Nifty MidCap index advanced 1.56% and the SmallCap index gained 0.54%. All NSE sectoral indices closed higher: FMCG rose 2.22%, Auto 1.36%, PSU Bank 1.41%, Private Bank 1.35%, and Media 1.23%. Only Oil and Gas lagged, ending as the worst-performing sector despite the wider rally. Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, ITC, and Eicher Motors were among the top Nifty gainers; TCS, Adani Ports, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Larsen & Toubro, and HDFC Bank all advanced, while Reliance Industries slipped.

IT Stocks Shake Off the Green-Card Shock

The standout was technology. The Nifty IT index surged over 3% as investors returned to the sector on optimism around second-quarter earnings and AI-linked revenue. TCS jumped more than 4% after reporting a 15% rise in September-quarter net profit to ₹13,884 crore, with AI-related revenue accelerating and international business growing. HCL Technologies rose 3.4% and Infosys gained 2.6%.

Remarkably, the rally came just a day after the Trump administration suspended Microsoft, Adobe, and major Indian IT firms — including TCS, Infosys, and Wipro — from the US Permanent Labor Certification program. TCS told investors the suspension would not materially affect its workforce strategy or client engagements, and the market took the company at its word. Reduced concerns about an imminent escalation between the United States and Iran also helped, alongside value buying and short covering after the recent correction.

Oil, Flows, and the Caveats

Softer crude prices did heavy lifting. Brent crude fell more than 1% to around $102.90 a barrel, retreating from evening highs above $105 — a meaningful tailwind for an economy that imports the bulk of its oil. "Softer crude prices and a firmer rupee provided additional support, although persistent FII selling and global uncertainties remain key risks," said Vikram Kasat, Chief Business Officer for Advisory and Dealing at PL Capital. Exchange data underscored the point: foreign institutional investors sold shares worth ₹12,943.58 crore on Thursday, with domestic institutions absorbing ₹10,703.11 crore of the outflow.

Analysts were careful not to declare a bottom. "Domestic equities staged a relief rally, supported by value buying and short covering after the recent sharp correction," market watchers noted — the word "relief" doing a lot of work. Elevated crude, continued foreign outflows, and tighter monetary policy remain overhangs. Gold rose more than 1% to ₹1,51,175 per 10 grams and silver gained 1.52% to ₹2,24,664 per kg, a sign that haven demand has not disappeared.

What Comes Next

Monday's domestic CPI print is the next test, offering the first hard data on the RBI's path after its shift to calibrated tightening — the October rate hike that triggered much of this month's volatility. After that, the second-quarter earnings season takes over: with Nifty 50 profits expected to grow around 20%, per analyst estimates, the rally's durability will depend on companies delivering, not just on oil prices cooperating. Asia ended mixed on Friday — Japan's Nikkei flat, Singapore lower, Hong Kong and Shanghai higher — and Wall Street closed mixed the night before. For now, Indian investors have their bounce; whether it becomes a trend is an earnings-season question.
